item.title: skill-up: How to Make Claude Work Your Way
item.description:
I talked about Agent Skills at the second Claude Code Helsinki meetup. It was good to see a crowd that size at a meetup.

Skills cost very few tokens up front. The model only loads one when it actually needs it. The rule of thumb I gave the room: if you find yourself prompting the LLM with the same thing over and over, that thing should be a skill.

Rather than just assert that skills are useful, I used one to build the talk. The slide deck was generated from scratch with Claude’s pptx skill, and I ran a live demo generating a deck from the Claude Code CLI.

What I covered

  • Why to use Agent Skills, now standardised as an open format at agentskills.io
  • How skills differ from MCP, hooks and plugins
  • The anatomy of a skill: SKILL.md, progressive disclosure, scripts and resources
  • Best practices
  • A live demo generating slides from the CLI

Thanks

Thanks to the Claude Code Helsinki organisers for having me.

item.title: From Prompt to Deployment in EKS
item.description:
I delivered a talk and live demo, “From Prompt to Deployment in EKS”, at AWS Community Day Nordics 2025 in Gothenburg. The subtitle says what it actually was: using the Amazon Q CLI and Model Context Protocol servers to get from a written request to a workload running on a cluster.

The demo ran live rather than from a recording, which is the only way to find out whether the tooling holds up.

It was a good day, and a memorable one for me. The lineup included a lot of people whose work I have followed for years.

Thanks

Thanks to the organising team, Sebastian Bille, Andreas Casen, Anurag Kale, Caroline Cah and Marcus Karlsson, and to the AWS Community Nordics volunteers.

item.title: AI Agents for Kubernetes Ops: Live incident recovery with MCP
item.description:
I presented “AI Agents for Kubernetes Ops: Live incident recovery with MCP” at AgentCon Helsinki. The live demo ran without any hiccups, thanks to Claude Sonnet 4 for not hallucinating too much.

The demo wired an agent built with the AWS Strands Agents SDK to a set of MCP servers and let it work a real incident on an Amazon EKS cluster end to end:

  • Inject a controlled pod error
  • Prometheus fires a rule to Alertmanager
  • The agent debugs the cluster through the EKS MCP server and writes an incident summary
  • It sends the summary by email through the SNS MCP server
  • It proposes a fix through the GitHub MCP server
  • After manual approval, it applies the patched Deployment via ArgoCD

The manual approval step is the part I would not remove. The interesting question is not whether an agent can produce a patch, it is where you put the human.

Thanks

Thanks to Siili Solutions for hosting, to Microsoft, and to the organisers Vesa Nopanen, Vesa Tikkanen, Anna Silvonen, Terho Antila, Vibha Deshpande and Teemu Lainiola for the opportunity.

item.title: Autonomous Troubleshooting on Amazon EKS with Strands Agents and MCP
item.description:
At AWS Summit Zurich I shared a view of where cloud operations is heading, along with an end-to-end demo: autonomous troubleshooting on Amazon EKS with Strands Agents and the Model Context Protocol.

Kubernetes troubleshooting has been automated for years. What is changing is that it is becoming autonomous. An agent can now hold enough context about a cluster to investigate a problem, not just execute a fixed runbook against it.

That shift is early, and this demo was one data point rather than a finished product. But agentic systems and open protocols like MCP are going to reshape how cloud operations works, and they move us closer to infrastructure that recovers on its own.

Thanks

Thanks to everyone who came to the session, and to the AWS community for the energy in the room.

item.title: Amazon EKS Auto Mode
item.description:
My talk at the AWS meetup in Helsinki, hosted at Accenture, on how EKS Auto Mode lets teams drop a lot of undifferentiated heavy lifting.

I started with the basics of Kubernetes for people new to it, then went through what EKS does for customers and how Auto Mode simplifies Day 2 operations. The Q&A was the best part, and I took as much from the audience’s perspectives as they took from the talk.

There is a longer writeup of this one on the blog: Presented on EKS Auto Mode at the AWS Helsinki Meetup.

Thanks

Thanks to Petri Rosenström, Rolf Koski and Accenture for organising the meetup.
